statement: If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the rectangle contained by the segments and the square on the aforesaid segment.
heath_proof: For let the straight line AB be cut at random at C; I say that the rectangle contained by AB, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by AC, CB together with the square on BC. For let the square CDEB be described on CB; [I. 46] let ED be drawn through to F, and through A let AF be drawn parallel to either CD or BE. [I. 31]  Then AE is equal to AD, CE. Now AE is the rectangle contained by AB, BC, for it is contained by AB, BE, and BE is equal to BC;   AD is the rectangle AC, CB, for DC is equal to CB; and DB is the square on CB. Therefore the rectangle contained by AB, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by AC, CB together with the square on BC.

2.3
**Statement:** If a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the rectangle contained by the segments and the square on the aforesaid segment.

Let AB be a straight line cut at random at the point C. I say that the rectangle contained by AB, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by AC, CB together with the square on CB.

**Step 1.** On CB describe the square CDEB [1.46], with CD and BE the sides standing on CB at C and B respectively, and DE the side opposite CB. Since CDEB is a square, its four sides CD, DE, EB, BC are equal to one another and its four angles DCB, CDE, DEB, EBC are right angles [D1.22].

**Step 2.** Since the angles DCB, CBE are right, the straight line CB falling on the two straight lines CD, BE makes the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles; therefore CD is parallel to BE [1.28]. In the same way, since the angles CDE, DCB are right, the straight line CD falling on DE, CB makes the interior angles on the same side equal to two right angles; therefore DE is parallel to CB [1.28].

**Step 3.** Produce ED beyond D [P2], and through the point A draw AF parallel to CD [1.31], F being the point in which AF meets ED produced. Since AF is parallel to CD, and CD is parallel to BE (Step 2), AF is also parallel to BE [1.30].

**Step 4.** In the quadrilateral AFEB, AF is parallel to BE (Step 3), and FE, which lies along the straight line DE, is parallel to AB, which lies along the straight line CB (Step 2); therefore AFEB is a parallelogram. Since AF is parallel to BE and AB falls on them, the angles FAB, ABE are together equal to two right angles [1.29]; but the angle ABE is the angle EBC of the square, which is right (Step 1); therefore the angle FAB is right. Likewise FE falls on the parallels AF, BE, so the angles AFE, FEB are together equal to two right angles [1.29]; the angle FEB is the angle DEB of the square, which is right (Step 1); therefore the angle AFE is right. Thus AFEB is a rectangular parallelogram, namely the rectangle contained by AB, BE [D2.1]; call it AE.

**Step 5.** In the quadrilateral ACDF, AF is parallel to CD (Step 3), and FD, which lies along ED, is parallel to AC, which lies along CB (Step 2); therefore ACDF is a parallelogram. Since AF is parallel to CD and AC falls on them, the angles FAC, ACD are together equal to two right angles [1.29]; but the angle FAC is the angle FAB, which is right (Step 4); therefore the angle ACD is right. Thus ACDF is a rectangular parallelogram, namely the rectangle contained by AC, CD [D2.1]; call it AD. Call the square CDEB also CE.

**Step 6.** The straight line CD divides the figure AE into the two figures AD and CE, and AE is made up of these two parts; therefore AE is equal to AD together with CE.

**Step 7.** Now AE is the rectangle contained by AB, BE (Step 4), and BE is equal to BC (Step 1); therefore AE is the rectangle contained by AB, BC. Again, AD is the rectangle contained by AC, CD (Step 5), and CD is equal to CB (Step 1); therefore AD is the rectangle contained by AC, CB. And CE is the square described on CB (Step 1).

**Step 8.** Therefore, by Step 6, the rectangle contained by AB, BC is equal to the rectangle contained by AC, CB together with the square on CB. Therefore, if a straight line be cut at random, the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the rectangle contained by the segments and the square on the aforesaid segment. Q.E.D.
